children: The suspension of green card-related labour certifications could raise employee retention and hiring costs, even as Indian IT companies reduce their reliance on US work visas

Indian IT services companies could face operating margin pressure of 10–30 basis points over the next 12 months following the US suspension of a key employment-based green card process. The impact is expected to stem from higher talent retention and workforce costs rather than an immediate loss of revenue.

The US Department of Labour’s October 8 decision to suspend Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) processing for eight technology companies has increased uncertainty for Indian IT services firms and their employees. While the move affects a route to permanent residency for foreign workers, companies have increasingly relied on local hiring and offshore delivery to reduce their dependence on immigration programmes.

Industry estimates suggest the financial impact could deepen if the suspension continues for several years. However, the near-term implications will depend on how affected companies manage employee retention, local recruitment and delivery costs.
Margin Pressure Could Build Over Time

According to media reports, the suspension could put operating margins under pressure by 10–30 basis points over the next 12 months. If the restrictions persist for several years, the pressure could increase to 30 to 75 basis points, while revenues could be 0.25 to 0.75 per cent below the levels otherwise expected.

The estimates indicate that the immediate impact on revenue could be negligible, with the principal risk arising from additional workforce-related expenses. Companies may need to offer stronger retention incentives, increase local hiring or rely more on subcontractors to maintain delivery commitments.

These are industry estimates rather than company-specific earnings forecasts. The actual impact will depend on the number of affected employees, the duration of the restrictions and the measures companies take to manage their US operations.
US Suspends PERM Processing For Eight Companies

The US administration announced the suspension on 8 October, covering Indian IT services companies Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Cognizant and Capgemini, along with US technology companies Microsoft and Adobe.

The US Department of Labour said it would stop accepting new applications and processing pending PERM applications involving the affected employers while investigations into alleged programme abuse continue. PERM certification is a key step in the employment-based green card process, requiring employers to demonstrate that qualified US workers are not available for the relevant position under applicable rules.

The suspension does not, by itself, amount to a blanket ban on H-1B visas. However, it creates uncertainty for employees seeking permanent residency through affected employers, particularly those whose immigration plans depend on the certification process.
Local Hiring And Offshore Delivery May Limit The Impact

Indian IT companies have reduced their dependence on employment-based immigration routes over the years, expanding local recruitment in the US and shifting more work to offshore delivery centres. This transition could limit the immediate effect of the suspension on their operations and earnings.

TCS, for instance, said its US workforce strategy would remain unaffected, citing the limited number of PERM applications it had submitted in the preceding two years. The company has also outlined plans to hire an additional 15,000 employees in the US over the next five years.

Nevertheless, according to media reports, analysts have flagged longer-term risks around talent retention, regulatory uncertainty and the potential for higher recruitment costs. Any extension of US scrutiny to other immigration or wage-related rules could add to those pressures.

The financial consequences will depend partly on whether the suspension remains limited to PERM processing or is followed by wider restrictions affecting foreign-worker recruitment. A prolonged freeze could make it harder for affected employees to secure permanent residency through their current employers, increasing the challenge of retaining experienced professionals.

For Indian IT companies, the issue is therefore not limited to the immediate cost of compliance. Higher employee turnover, replacement hiring and changes to workforce deployment could affect delivery economics over time. The estimated margin impact remains contingent on how the situation develops and how companies adjust their staffing strategies.
